series_label: Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)
source_or_custodian: World Development Indicators (WB_WDI); source: Trends in Maternal Mortality, Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, World Bank Group, and UNDESA/Population Division)
status_or_notes: Modeled estimates. The series covers 1985-2023, so the server has no values for 2024-2025. Metadata limitation: the methodology differs from that used for previous estimates, so data should not be compared historically; maternal mortality ratios are generally of unknown reliability. SDG indicator 3.1.1. The server also has a separate national-estimate series, WB_WDI_SH_STA_MMRT_NE, which was not used here.
definition: Maternal mortality ratio is the number of women who die from pregnancy-related causes while pregnant or within 42 days of pregnancy termination per 100,000 live births. The data are estimated with a regression model using information on the proportion of maternal deaths among non-AIDS deaths in women ages 15-49, fertility, birth attendants, and GDP measured using purchasing power parities (PPPs).
